note: The BATTLE screen's layout and the runtime fields it may show. Layout numbers are PRODUCT-AUTHORED for a 9:16 phone frame. Every HUD field below is traced to a ROM read site, so the screen shows what the original tracks and nothing else. This file lives with the contracts rather than in src/ because src/championship carries no binary asset paths at all.

open: full action and child object graph

frame.note: The original is a two-screen portrait stack: two 256x192 screens, 256x384 together, ratio 0.667. Every ROM background witness comes in a _main / _sub pair, battle_result included, so the original used both screens on every screen including battle. That is evidence for a PORTRAIT ORIENTATION and nothing more. The five bands below, their order and their exact heights are a PRODUCT-AUTHORED re-arrangement: no ROM layout has been traced for them, and saying they are what the second screen carried would overstate what the witnesses prove.
frame.orientationDecisionNote: The Owner confirmed 9:16 on 2026-09-02 after the arena art appeared letterboxed. The dark bands were an unbuilt screen, not a wrong aspect: the arena renders are 3:2, which fills the field band exactly, and 16:9 would have matched neither the 3:2 art nor the original's 4:3 screens.

bands.note: 0.375 of a 9:16 frame at full width is exactly 3:2, which is the aspect the arena renders are authored at. Full-bleed horizontally; no crop.

This milestone is VS5 Auto Battle, and the trace agrees: the AI selects for all six slots and no traced site takes player input during a match. So this band is a record of what happened, not a command menu. A command menu here would imply an interaction the original does not have.

teams.note: OVL19 0x0210CAB8 indexes slot = withinTeam + base and advances base by 3 per team, so the six slots the frame walks are two teams laid end to end.

notShown.note: Fields the screen deliberately does not draw, so nobody adds them later believing they were forgotten.
notShown.accuracy: The original resolves contact, not accuracy. There is no hit/miss roll to show.
notShown.damageNumbers: No traced site produces a per-hit number for display. The resolver writes HP; whether the original drew a number is a presentation question this lane has not answered.
notShown.turnOrder: There are no turns. Six slots dispatch per frame until one engages, and cooldowns pace them.
notShown.commandMenu: The battle is automatic. The AI selection module chooses for every slot, and no traced site reads player input between the start of a match and its verdict.

arenaArt.note: No art path is declared here. Licensed arena pixels load through the production index and main.js. Declaring a path would put a loadable URL on a file that src/ imports. The scene draws product-authored neutral technical art when those pixels are absent.

layerModel.note: ARM9 0x020CC148, 11 records of 0x18. Each arena names its own field, a shared common layer, an optional animated layer and an optional object layer. Ten of the eleven share one common layer; BATTLE_CYBERSPACE has none, which is why its frame does not match the others.

fields.string08: the shared common layer, empty only for BATTLE_CYBERSPACE
fields.string0C: an animated layer, present on BATTLE_VOLCANO and BATTLE_ISLAND only
fields.string10: an object layer, present on four arenas

standPositions.note: Where the six combatants stand on the field is not decided here. States 4 and 5 carry the approach geometry and are blocked on a world-position model and the DS math routine at 0x02003098. The scene lays the six out evenly as PRODUCT-AUTHORED placement and says so; it is not a claim about the original.
